outcome: secondary arrest of dilatation and descent
cohort: 400 pregnant women in active labor (cervical dilation >= 4cm) recruited by random sampling from the labor room of a hospital in Udaipur, India.
finding: The paperless partogram was found to be effective and user-friendly in the management of labor and prevention of abnormal or prolonged labor compared to the WHO partogram in low-risk cases.
mod_finding: 94.75% of participants had a normal vaginal delivery and 5.25% had a lower segment cesarean section (LSCS).
